concepts.why: Secular scholar / Jewish reader / Reformed and Orthodox alike: the concept is the question 'what is man that You are mindful of him?'. Hebrews 2:9 does not ask it; it applies the phrase 'a little lower than the angels' to Jesus. Set under this name it reads as Psalm 8 being about Him, which is the OT-points-to-NT grouping the site must not make. Hebrews 2:6-7 (the quotation itself) stays and is enough; the Christ application is already carried by concept 11.

concepts.name: Dust (or: For dust you are)
concepts.why: Secular scholar / Baptist / Wesleyan: the name 'He is mindful that we are dust' is Psalm 103:14, but only that verse says God is mindful. Genesis 2:7, 3:19, 18:27 and Ecclesiastes 3:20 and 12:7 say man is dust and say nothing of God's attention, so the name says more than five of its six passages. Rename to a plain label ('Dust') or a phrase every passage holds. 'For dust you are' is Genesis 3:19's own words but Genesis 2:7 and 18:27 do not say 'return', so the plain label 'Dust' is the safest. All six notes are exact quotations and stay.

concepts.name: Adam (or: The first man Adam)
concepts.why: Secular scholar / Jewish reader of Genesis / Catholic and Orthodox: 'the last Adam' is said only by 1 Corinthians 15:45. Genesis 2:7, Genesis 5:3 and Luke 3:38 speak of Adam and say nothing of a last one; under this name they are read as the first half of a pair, i.e. Genesis pointing to Christ. 'The first man Adam' is also 1 Corinthians 15:45's wording and is true of all six passages without making the pairing the concept's name; 'Adam' is the plain label. The notes on Romans 5:14 and 1 Corinthians 15 carry Paul's pairing in his own words and stay. (Name only; passages and notes unchanged.)

secondary_or_links: Moses' face -> the veil over his face: trim 2 Corinthians 3:13-16 to 2 Corinthians 3:13. The concept is the veil over Moses' face; verses 14-16 (the veil 'at the reading of the old covenant', 'only in Christ can it be removed') go beyond it and put the Old Testament under the New, which Jewish readers of the Hebrew Bible and secular scholars would take as a side. Verse 13 holds the veil and stays. (If 3:16 is wanted for 'the veil is taken away', keep 3:13 and 3:16 only, not 14-15.)

Kingdom -> priests: kept as the verbal link it is (Exodus 19:6, Revelation 1:6; 1 Peter 2:9 says 'royal priesthood', as the drafter notes). This is the place where Israel-and-church readers differ (dispensational Baptists above all). It is acceptable only because the name and the arrow state two words and no claim that one people is the other; the entry must carry no note joining Exodus 19:6 to 1 Peter 2:9.
All other secondary concepts accepted: each is a verbal link in the texts' words. The 'Links to other themes' list is acceptable as given.
All notes I checked against the packet's verse texts are exact quotations of their verses; no note fixes needed.
